purpose: Test whether a running run can expose explicitly recorded data plus progress/readiness markers that user scripts or live monitors can consume before the run finishes, while keeping automated fit/advice, scan mutation, and autonomous calibration out of the base claim.

user_refinement: near-term need is reading already recorded data from a running run and knowing the completeness/readiness of the relevant analysis unit
a live monitor may show latest data and simple cursor/range-fit previews, but Scopecat does not need to record every intermediate UI operation
experiment code should record data, sweep semantics, lifecycle events, and decision-relevant context into Scopecat
prompt_method_check: blind role-play suggested passive advisory feedback and more aggressive adaptive scan behavior; this fixture treats those as later hypotheses
external_baseline: existing frameworks already cover acquisition, plotting, callbacks, dashboards, scheduling, or calibration in their own stacks
future_hypotheses_out_of_scope: automated fit execution as a required first slice

artifacts.role: explicitly recorded partial sweep slices and lifecycle events
running-run progress and readiness index for scripts and monitors
simple live-monitor capability and recording boundary
optional later automated quality/anomaly decision evidence
optional later recorded-input replay check for the same decision packet

fixture_questions: Can explicit partial-sweep recording tell users which recorded data is available and which analysis units are fit-ready while the run continues?
Can ordinary scripts and a simple live monitor consume the same running-run progress/readiness index?
Which saved fit or operator-decision artifacts, if any, should become durable evidence?
Which later ideas remain outside the first slice: automated fit execution, replayable advice, adaptive scan mutation, or append-style scan plans?
